subject: Communication
title: Psychological Safety: Leading by Listening
description: One-minute skill: Psychological Safety: Leading by Listening.

hook.text: Google studied 180 teams to find what made the best ones. Number one factor?

buildup.text: Amy Edmondson defined psychological safety: a shared belief that the team is safe for risk-taking and speaking up.

discovery.text: Leaders create psychological safety through listening: asking questions, acknowledging concerns, and responding openly.

twist.text: A leader who says 'my door is always open' but checks their phone during conversations destroys psychological safety.

climax.text: The highest-performing teams aren't the smartest. They're the ones where everyone feels heard.

punchline.text: Teams don't fail from lack of talent. They fail when people stop speaking up.

quiz.question: What did Google's research find was the #1 factor in team effectiveness?

details.summary: Psychological safety, the belief that you will not be punished for speaking up, is created primarily through how leaders listen. When people feel heard without judgment, they share ideas, admit mistakes, and raise concerns.
details.whyItMatters: Psychological safety is built one listening interaction at a time. The way you respond when someone speaks up determines whether others ever will.
takeaways: Psychological safety is the top predictor of team performance
It is built through non-judgmental, attentive listening
Google's Project Aristotle confirmed its critical importance

faq.question: What is Google's Project Aristotle?
faq.answer: A multi-year Google study of 180 teams to identify what makes teams effective. The top factor was not intelligence, experience, or resources but psychological safety. Teams where members felt safe to take risks and be vulnerable consistently outperformed all others.

faq.question: How quickly can psychological safety be destroyed?
faq.answer: A single punitive response to vulnerability can destroy months of built trust. Publicly shaming someone for an honest mistake, dismissing an idea sarcastically, or retaliating against feedback teaches the entire team that speaking up is dangerous. Recovery takes far longer than destruction.
